title: Soft failover attenuation with KV consistency for streamed sessions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement an active-active soft failover mechanism at the hosted API edge that 1) shifts traffic gradually across regions, 2) preserves streaming session continuity with bounded staleness using KV cache checkpoints, 3) integrates with our circuit breaker and load-shedding policies to protect origin capacity, and 4) provides observable SLO impact and rollback controls. Scope: edge/gateway layer (regional gateways + egress proxies), session metadata propagation, KV checkpointing hooks, traffic attenuation controller, and console runbook. Out of scope: control-plane-only routing experiments, Dedicated-specific autoscaling controls. Success criteria: (a) failover completes without hard-terminating >99% of live streams within a 5m window, (b) 99th-percentile request latency degradation <= 30% during attenuation, (c) no SLO violations for non-failing regions beyond 1 hour, (d) automated rollback triggers on sustained error-rate or token-drop thresholds. Key trade-offs: stronger consistency requires more frequent KV flushes (increases latency and cost); softer attenuation reduces cold-start risk but extends dual-writing pressure. We prioritize user-perceived continuity for streaming customers while bounding cost and origin pressure.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha K.: Initial ticket created after postmortem for incident #2025-02-edge-12. Proposal includes a phased attenuation controller and KV checkpoint metadata attached to session cookies.

2025-02-18 - Daniel M.: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype attenuation controller that applies per-route weights and a 'stream-handoff' header. Observed ~12% latency increase when KV flush frequency moved from 60s->10s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2187

2025-02-22 - Design review (Lina T.): Suggested exposing attenuation curve in Console with presets (fast, balanced, conservative) and a streaming-safe toggle. Also recommended UX copy for rollback actions.
2025-02-25 - Security (E. Park): Confirmed no sensitive payloads are written into KV snapshots; encryption-in-transit & KMS in place. No additional controls required for this change.

2025-03-01 - Daniel M.: Running chaos simulations in staging (packet loss + region flaps). Observed that circuit-breaker 'fast-open' at 5% error rate reduced origin overload but increased session drop rate when paired with aggressive attenuation. Next: introduce coordination between attenuation controller and circuit-breaker to bias attenuation before circuit-open triggers.

2025-03-02 - PM (Ravi S.): Approved schedule for gradual rollout to 10% of traffic in canary regions, with dashboarding for SLO, stream-drop-count, and KV-lag. Add runbook steps for manual restore and gather SRE on-call for first rollouts.
implementation_notes: Design summary: 1) Attenuation controller computes per-region egress weights using SLO-preserving heuristics (latency headroom, token-rate, KV-lag). 2) Streaming sessions annotated with KV-checkpoint IDs and 'handoff-timestamp' to allow rehydration in target region. 3) Circuit-breaker exposes a 'pressure' signal (0..1) to attenuation controller; pressure>0.6 triggers accelerated attenuation and temporary session-accept filters. 4) Load-shedding policy prefers short-lived requests over long-running streaming connections when origin capacity is constrained. Observability: add token-level metrics, per-session handoff success, kv-sync-lag histogram, and attenuation-step timeline. Rollout plan: unit tests -> integration tests with session continuity harness -> staging canary (10%) -> regional ramp (25/50/100) with SLO monitors and automatic pause on error budget burn.
qa_checklist: 1) End-to-end simulated failover with 1k concurrent streams: verify >=99% sessions recover within 5 minutes. 2) KV checkpoint rehydration test across region pair with artificial lag. 3) Circuit-breaker coordination test: create synthetic errors to exercise coordinated acceleration. 4) Load-shedding acceptance criteria: under high load, short requests maintain 80% of baseline throughput. 5) Console: attenuation UI works and rollback button succeeds.
next_steps: 1) Finalize attenuation curve parameters and expose presets in Console (owner: Design). 2) Implement coordinated pressure API between circuit-breaker and attenuation controller (owner: Edge). 3) Add KV checkpoint persistence hook to session lifecycle (owner: Runtime). 4) Build end-to-end test harness for streaming continuity (owner: SRE). 5) Schedule canary and include SRE/Oncall in rollout window.
notes_for_review: Focus reviewers on: (a) whether attenuation presets match customer class expectations, (b) any missing telemetry that would prevent safe rollback, (c) edge cases for cross-region rehydration when upstream model variant mismatch exists.
